name: Dumbbell Curl
description: The dumbbell curl trains the biceps brachii and brachialis using independent dumbbells, allowing the wrist to supinate freely through the range of motion which maximizes biceps activation. It can be performed with both arms simultaneously or alternating, and the independent loading helps identify and correct biceps strength imbalances.

execution.starting_position: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides with a neutral or supinated grip, elbows against the sides.
execution.setup_instructions: Can be performed seated or standing. Seated reduces the temptation to use body swing.
steps: Curl one dumbbell (or both) upward, rotating the wrist to full supination as the dumbbell rises.
Fully contract the bicep at the top.
Lower under control, rotating back to neutral if alternating.
Repeat on the other side if alternating.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Using body swing to lift the dumbbell
Not fully supinating the forearm during the curl
safety_considerations: If using alternating technique, maintain a neutral wrist at the bottom
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension at the bottom with full supination at the top.
coaching_cues: Turn the pinky toward the ceiling at the top to maximize supination
Keep the elbow pinned — it should not drive forward
